events.what: Tall proves the Scholz conjecture for an infinite family of integers with v(n)=7 and l(2n)=l(n); later published in INTEGERS 24A
Agama's much-revised preprint giving a conditional upper bound on l(2^n-1) under a 'carry degree' condition not shown to hold for any specific n
events.credibility_reason: 12 versions over 4.5 years; result conditional on an unverified hypothesis

events.what: Agama defines closed addition chains and proves the Scholz inequality for 'complete numbers' for which these chains are optimal
events.credibility_reason: Unreviewed note on the Cryptology ePrint Archive by an author with a long-revised conditional preprint on the same problem; the class is newly defined by an optimality hypothesis, and the record's researcher read only the abstract, so it is unclear whether the class is non-trivial or explicitly known to be infinite

judgement.doubts: The partial status rests only on the Agama 2025 ePrint note. It is unreviewed and was read only at abstract level. Its 'complete numbers' are defined by the hypothesis that closed chains are optimal, so the case settled may be narrow or hard to exhibit. Tall's refereed v(n)=7 result is pre-snapshot (arXiv Oct 2022) and cannot set the status. If Agama 2025 were set aside, the status would be open.

corrections.why: F5 (retained with doubt): the status rests only on Agama's unreviewed ePrint 2025/833. The record says it read only abstracts ('I did not read the full proof sections'). The 'complete numbers' class is defined by an optimality condition, so the scope may be thin. Doubtful but not not_credible: the record identifies no error and there are not several F5 signals.
